paragraphs: The straitjacket is one of the few garments that reads instantly as a story rather than as clothing. Arms crossed and buckled, movement removed: it belongs to psychiatric history, to horror and to stage work, and adding fur turns it from a clinical object into a deliberately unsettling one.
The figure holds 71,133 polygons and 71,456 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied as a static pose. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $169 it suits horror and thriller film work, game characters, theatre and costume previsualisation, editorial illustration and concept art. On sale since 2025.

Every culture that invented a dragon gave it wings eventually, and the flying pose is the one that carries the myth. Wings held out, body extended, tail trailing as a counterweight: it is a shape borrowed from birds and bats and made larger than either could ever be.

The creature holds 50,837 polygons and 50,649 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, kept light enough for real time use, and carries StemCell certification so it moves cleanly between engines.
At $169 it suits game creatures, fantasy film and animation, tabletop and card art, book covers and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

A dry dock is a hole in the coastline with gates. Flood it, float the ship in, pump it out, and the hull sits on blocks with a hundred metres of steel suddenly standing in open air. It is the only place a ship's underside is ever seen, and everything about the structure exists to make that possible.

The scene runs 1,606,712 polygons and 1,693,279 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, covering the dock structure and its surrounding yard equipment. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $169 it suits shipbuilding and maritime visualisation, industrial and infrastructure scenes, documentary and film, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Kibo is the largest single module on the International Space Station and the only one with an external platform and its own airlock, so experiments can be pushed out into vacuum and pulled back without a spacewalk. The robotic arm on its exterior does that work.

The module holds 463,366 polygons and 501,989 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 20 maps all at 4096x4096, and carries StemCell certification. A rigged build of the science module is offered separately.
At $169 it suits space programme visualisation, documentary and news graphics, museum and education work, simulation, film and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

Zvezda was the station's first home. It supplied the life support, the propulsion and the crew quarters that made the ISS habitable at all, and its design lineage runs straight back to the Mir core. For years, everything else was built around it.

The model holds 697,727 polygons and 774,001 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in the fully assembled configuration with its external fittings. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $169 it suits space programme visualisation, documentary and news graphics, museum and education work, simulation, film and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

An LCAC does not land, it arrives. Riding on a cushion of air, it crosses the surf line and keeps going up the beach, which means a force can be put ashore on ground that would stop a conventional landing craft entirely. The skirt is what makes that possible and what makes the craft unmistakable.
The model holds 26,897 polygons over 292,030 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification for use across engines and renderers.
At $169 it suits military and naval visualisation, defence presentation, documentary and film, simulation, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

An LNG plant exists to make a gas small enough to ship. Cooled to the point where it becomes liquid, natural gas shrinks by hundreds of times, and the sprawl of exchangers, columns and spherical tanks on the site is entirely in service of that one refrigeration problem.

The scene runs 1,154,223 polygons and 1,416,709 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, covering the process units, tanks and supporting structures. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $169 it suits energy and infrastructure visualisation, oil and gas presentation, training and safety material, documentary and news graphics, film and game environments. On sale since 2025.

The hospital gown is a garment nobody chooses. It opens at the back because access matters more than dignity, and the moment a figure is wearing one, the viewer knows the setting without being told. That shorthand is what makes it useful in healthcare imagery.
The figure holds 79,859 polygons and 80,256 vertices in quads and tris, with mixed UV layout across the parts, supplied as a static pose. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $169 it suits healthcare and hospital visualisation, medical education and patient material, pharmaceutical presentation, editorial illustration and film previsualisation. On sale since 2026.

Mining kit has not changed in principle for a century: a light on the helmet, a self rescuer on the belt, boots that survive water. The tools around the figure explain the job better than the figure alone, which is why a collection works here where a single character would not.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the miner together with the accessories as static pieces. It is built to CheckMate specification.

At $169 the set suits mining and resources visualisation, safety and training material, industrial presentation, documentary and film, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The Mercury was Henry Dreyfuss designing a train the way one would design an object: streamlined shell, integrated lighting, an observation lounge. New York Central built it from rebuilt commuter stock, which makes it one of the few famous streamliners assembled largely from what was already lying around.

The model is exceptionally dense at 5,062,069 polygons and 5,149,335 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, capturing the streamlined bodywork and running gear. It is built to CheckMate specification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $169 it suits railway and transport history visualisation, museum and exhibition work, documentary and film, period scenes and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A bench with someone on it changes a public space from an architectural drawing into a place. An elderly woman sitting is the most ordinary version of that, and ordinary is exactly what most park, plaza and street renders are missing.
The figure holds 40,740 polygons and 41,673 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, light enough to place several in one scene, and carries StemCell certification.
At $159 it suits architectural and urban visualisation, landscape and public space renders, healthcare and social material, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A gas carrier is recognisable from the horizon by the domes on its deck: pressure tanks that hold the cargo cold and contained, sitting proud of the hull because that is the only shape that works. No other class of ship looks like it.

The vessel holds 1,145,448 polygons and 1,160,044 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 40 maps, 10 at 8192x8192, 27 at 4096x4096, one at 2048x2048 and two at 1024x1024. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a generic build without markings is offered separately.
At $159 it suits energy and shipping visualisation, port and infrastructure scenes, documentary and news graphics, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2017.

Karate is codified to an unusual degree: the stances have names, the positions are taught identically across schools, and a fighter mid technique is holding a shape that is meant to be recognisable. A collection captures that range where one figure could only ever show a single moment.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the fighters as static poses. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.

At $159 the set suits sports and martial arts visualisation, game characters, instructional and educational material, advertising, film previsualisation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2017.

The GLI is the Jetta that borrows from the Golf GTI: the same turbocharged engine and the same suspension work, wrapped in a saloon body that draws less attention. It exists for people who want the performance without announcing it, and Monterey Blue Pearl is about as loud as it gets.

The model holds 215,612 polygons and 238,598 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, and comes rigged so the wheels, doors and steering can be posed or animated. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $149 it suits automotive marketing and configurators, street and architectural scenes, advertising, film and television, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.
